Zong Chuke, Wu Sansi, Wu Yanxiu, and their allies were then taking turns as court factions. Riyong quietly attached himself to each in turn and was rapidly promoted to Vice Minister of War and concurrently a Xiuwen Hall academician.
修文館 is Xiuwen Hall; Xiuxian misreads 文 as 仙.

Learning that Prince Lin (the future Xuanzong) was planning a coup, he used the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye as intermediaries to visit the prince's residence in secret, pledged himself deeply, and plotted to help place him on the throne.

Learning that Xuanzong was planning a righteous rising, he used the monk Purun and the Daoist Wang Ye as intermediaries to visit the princely residence in secret, pledged himself deeply, and plotted to support and elevate him.
The unit names 玄宗 and 義舉; Prince Lin and 'coup' are not in the Chinese.
He was soon sent out as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as prefect of Wu and Bian, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Senior Administrator of Jingzhou.
He was soon sent out as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou, then served in turn as prefect of Wuzhou and Bianzhou, Military Commissioner of Yanzhou, and Senior Administrator of Jingzhou.
婺州 and 汴州 are Wuzhou and Bianzhou; bare Wu invites confusion with 吳.
At twenty he took the Five Classics examination, was appointed magistrate of Pingxiang, but was dismissed for an offense and returned home.
At twenty he took the Five Classics examination, was appointed commandant of Pingxiang, but was dismissed for an offense and returned home.
平鄉尉 is a county commandant (尉), not a magistrate (令).

My younger brother Jiayou has just been appointed Vice Prefect of Binzhou; we are posted to opposite ends of the empire, united in heart yet separated in body, our spirits torn apart by ten thousand li.

My younger brother Jiayou has just been appointed Vice Prefect of Shanzhou; we are posted to opposite ends of the empire, united in heart yet separated in body, our spirits torn apart by ten thousand li.
鄯州 is Shanzhou; Binzhou would be 邠州.
My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Bin; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart yet dwelling apart, our spirits severed by ten thousand li.
My younger brother Jiayou is now appointed Vice Prefect of Shan; he and I are each in a different region—of one heart yet dwelling apart, our spirits severed by ten thousand li.
The same 鄯州 error appears in the literal English as Bin.
Soon afterward Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Xianxian was imprisoned; the Emperor asked his ministers what sentence was appropriate, and Jiazhen again petitioned for corporal punishment.
Soon afterward Military Commissioner of Guangzhou Pei Zhouxian was imprisoned; the Emperor asked his ministers what sentence was appropriate, and Jiazhen again petitioned for corporal punishment.
伷 is Zhou, so 裴伷先 is Pei Zhouxian, not Xianxian.
Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear mourning dress and await judgment, barring him from court audience; Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.
Zhang Yue urged Jiazhen to wear plain dress and await judgment, barring him from court audience; Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Youzhou, and Yue replaced him as Director of the Secretariat.
素服待罪 is plain dress while awaiting punishment, not mourning clothes.
The Emperor was moved as well and immediately summoned the youth, bestowing the name Yanbao and specially appointing him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.
The Emperor was moved as well and immediately summoned the youth, bestowing the name Yanshang and specially appointing him Military Staff Officer of the Left Inner Rate.
延賞 is Yanshang; Yanbao would require 寶.

Since the Kaiyuan reign more than ten Xiangzhou prefects had died or been demoted in office. Jiayou learned that Yuwen Jiong had served as area commander of Xiang at the end of the Northern Zhou and died for the state, and he established a shrine to Jiong's spirit to seek divine protection.

Since the Kaiyuan reign more than ten Xiangzhou prefects had died or been demoted in office. Jiayou learned that Yuchi Jiong had served as area commander of Xiang at the end of the Northern Zhou and died for the state, and he established a shrine to Jiong's spirit to seek divine protection.
尉遲 is the surname Yuchi; Yuwen is 宇文.
Later, when Wu Jing became prefect of Ye, he added imperial regalia to Yuwen's spirit image as well.
Later, when Wu Jing became prefect of Ye, he added imperial regalia to Yuchi's spirit image as well.
尉遲神 continues the same surname Yuchi, not Yuwen.
Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.
Xiao Song was the great-grandnephew of Xiao Yu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Duke of Song in early Zhenguan.
左僕射 is the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (尚書), not of the Secretariat.
When Han Xiu became chief minister he was stern and upright and would not defer to Song; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.
When Han Xiu became chief minister, Song took the initiative in handling business; Xiu was stern and upright and would not defer to him; they argued before the Emperor until Song offered to resign.
嵩舉事 is omitted in the original, a real gap, but 'Song raised affairs' is awkward English.
The following autumn Tibet invaded in force; Ximoming again led troops against Guazhou, but Shougui drove them off.
The following autumn Tibet invaded in force; Ximoming then led troops against Guazhou, but Shougui drove them off.
In the supplied window 悉末明 has not previously attacked; 復 here is sequential 'then', not a second Ximoming campaign.
Xiao Hua, Song's son Hua, at the end of Tianbao was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
Xiao Hua, at the end of Tianbao, was transferred to Vice Minister of War.
蕭華子華 names Xiao Hua; Song is not in this sentence, so 'Song's son Hua' is an insertion.
Hua's sons were Heng and Wu.
Hua's sons were Chang and Wu.
恆 is Hua's son, distinct from 衡 in the previous sentence; rendering both as Heng fuses two men. Chang keeps them apart in English.
Heng's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era (827–835).
Chang's son Fu became chief minister in the Dahe era (827–835).
恆子俯 is the son of Hua's son 恆, not 衡's son 復 of s0207.
The Emperor replied, "Do not, like Wang Yifu who recognized Shi Le too late, mistakenly harm a loyal man."
The Emperor replied, "Do not use the anecdote of Wang Yifu recognizing Shi Le and thereby mistakenly harm a loyal man."
王夷甫知石勒故事 cites that anecdote; it does not say Wang recognized Shi Le too late.

He soon requested leave to visit his parents' tombs, fell ill on the journey, and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenxian ("Literary Exemplar").

He soon requested leave to return and pay respects at the graves, then fell ill and died at sixty-eight. He was posthumously made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Wenxian ("Literary Exemplar").
歸拜墓 does not say parents, and 因遇疾卒 does not say he fell ill on the journey; those are real inventions. The proposed line is still abrupt and drops the useful Wenxian gloss.
E Prefect Cui Fa insulted a junior eunuch attendant, provoking Emperor Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed over to the censorate for investigation.
Magistrate Cui Fa of Hu County insulted a junior eunuch attendant, provoking Emperor Jingzong's fierce anger; he was handed over to the censorate for investigation.
鄠縣令 is magistrate of Hu County, not E Prefect.

In the ninth year of Dahe, as Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, when ministers and generals who had been implicated were slaughtered en masse, Zhongfang secretly ordered their bodies identified.
將相從累者 are implicated ministers and generals; the Sweet Dew name is not in the Chinese.

Soldiers were running rampant at the time, and Zhongfang was regarded as too mild and ineffectual for the crisis. He was found unfit for office, appointed governor of Hua Prefecture, and later transferred to be Director of the Palace Library.
秘書監 is Director of the Palace Library, not of the Secretariat.

Li Shizhi, also named Chang, was a grandson of Prince of Hengshan Chengqian.
李適之 appears once; the repeated 'Li Shizhi—' has no source.

When Supervising Secretary Han Chaozong was serving as an inspection commissioner, he singled Shizhi out in a memorial of recommendation, and Shizhi was promoted to Area Commander of Qin Prefecture.
給事中 is Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not an official 'of the Secretariat'.
Li Jiqing, styled Zi Jiqing, passed the Mingjing examination in his youth and showed considerable talent for literary composition.
His son Li Jiqing passed the Mingjing examination in his youth and showed considerable talent for literary composition.
After Shizhi's death, 子 marks Li Jiqing as his son; it is not a courtesy name Zi Jiqing.
Li Jiqing—Zi Jiqing—at the age of weak cap passed the Mingjing examination and was quite skilled in literary composition.
His son Li Jiqing, at the age of weak cap, passed the Mingjing examination and was quite skilled in literary composition.

His grandson Li Rong was upright and disciplined by nature and skilled in administrative affairs.
孫 marks Li Rong as grandson, not a courtesy name Sun Rong.

His grandson Li Rong had a nature upright and strict and was skilled in administrative affairs.

His uncle Fang Ni served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue during the Jingyun era.
方嶷 is Fang Ni; Fangyan misreads 嶷.

His uncle Fang Ni, in the Jingyun period, was Langzhong in the Ministry of Revenue.

He took the special imperial examination and passed in Broad Learning and Eloquent Composition, then rose twice to the post of commandant of Hu County in the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.

Wang Maozhong, Director of the Palace Administration, had been sent to Taiyuan, Shuofang, and You to audit troops and horses. Years passed, and he then sent an official dispatch to Taiyuan demanding arms and equipment.
王毛仲 is Wang Maozhong; 殿中監 is Director of the Palace Administration, not the Palace Domestic Service.

In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, Wang Maozhong fell from favor and was ordered to die. Xuanzong remembered Tingzhi's earlier memorial, promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice, and showed him deep favor before appointing him Director of the Grand Treasury.
二十年 in this Kaiyuan narrative is Kaiyuan 20, and 毛仲 is Maozhong, not Maoqi.
